criteria.text: Given a customer selects a field and time, when they confirm booking, then the booking is recorded.
Given a field is already booked, when a customer tries to book it, then they receive a conflict message.

stories.notes: In-memory booking store (no DB yet, per this story's scope). Idempotent create: an identical repeat request from the same customer returns the existing booking instead of erroring or duplicating; a genuine conflict (different customer or non-matching overlapping time) returns 409. All 3 criteria verified via automated tests (backend unit/route tests, frontend interaction tests using userEvent) plus manual curl checks and a live browser check against real dev servers.

criteria.text: Given a refund request, when it is flagged as important, then it is sent to a human for approval.
Given a complaint is received, when it is flagged as important, then it is sent to a human for approval.
Trust: All escalations to humans are logged with timestamps and decision outcomes.

stories.notes: Every valid refund/complaint request is escalated to a human (REQ-008 treats refunds/complaints themselves as the important decisions, no separate triage story exists yet to do finer filtering). In-memory store, no DB yet, same deliberate scope choice as STORY-001/002. Both creation and decision are idempotent: an identical repeat request or an identical repeat decision does not double-create or double-process (double-processing an approval is a real double-refund risk, not just a nicety here). A conflicting second decision (different outcome or decider) on an already-decided escalation is rejected (409), not silently overwritten. All 3 criteria verified via automated tests plus manual curl checks and a live check against real dev servers.

criteria.text: Given a new booking overlaps an existing one, when the system checks, then it identifies a conflict.
Given no overlap exists, when the system checks, then it confirms no conflict.
Trust: All conflict checks are logged with booking details.

stories.notes: Conflict detection logic already existed inline inside createBooking() since STORY-002; this story extracted it into its own explicit, reusable, independently-tested checkForConflict() function and added dedicated logging covering both outcomes (STORY-002 only ever logged the success/creation case, never the check itself). createBooking() now calls checkForConflict() rather than duplicating the overlap logic. All 3 named failure paths handled with dedicated tests: 'Missed conflict' (a real overlap is caught), 'False positive conflict' (a cancelled booking or a non-overlapping/adjacent time never falsely flags), 'Logging failure' (a broken logger cannot crash the check - wrapped in try/catch, verified via a test that makes console.log throw and confirms the check still returns the correct result). Refactoring this exposed a pre-existing test-hygiene issue in bookingsService.test.ts: two audit-logging tests used a manual logSpy.mockRestore() at the end of each test body, which never ran when an assertion failed partway through, leaking the spy's call history into the next test; fixed by switching to afterEach(() => jest.restoreAllMocks()). No frontend work - task guidance scopes this to 'the booking service', and the existing BookingForm (STORY-002) already surfaces conflict errors from its UI.

criteria.text: Given a booking is made, when the booking is confirmed, then the booking details are recorded in the audit trail.
Given a booking is cancelled, when the cancellation is processed, then the cancellation details are recorded in the audit trail.
Trust: Given any booking action occurs, when the action is completed, then the action is logged with a timestamp in the audit trail.

stories.notes: No cancellation capability existed before this story (STORY-002 only ever built creation); added a minimal cancelBooking() as a necessary walking-skeleton prerequisite for auditing a cancellation action, since the acceptance criteria explicitly require one. Audit trail is a real structured, queryable store (recordAuditEntry/listAuditEntries), distinct from the console logging STORY-001/002/004 already do - that logging isn't 'accessible for verification' in any structured sense, this is, via GET /api/audit-trail. Both creation and cancellation are idempotent, and cancellation is idempotent-verified at the audit-trail level too: cancelling twice does not add a duplicate entry. No frontend UI built for this story - the acceptance criteria and task guidance are satisfied at the API level ('accessible for verification' = the GET endpoint), and unlike STORY-001/004 nothing here names a customer- or staff-facing page; the owning role is System Auditor, not a UI persona. All 3 criteria verified via automated tests plus manual curl checks (including confirming the audit trail entry count stayed at 2, not 3, after a repeat cancellation) against a live dev server.
